releases.notes:
Updates could stop arriving, and the appliance would not say so.

ASCIA deliberately holds Home Assistant's supporting components at versions it has tested
together, rather than taking whatever is newest. Home Assistant reads that as "somebody has fallen
behind and should catch up", and refuses to install anything until they do — so an appliance could
sit with an update already downloaded and installed on it, and quietly decline to apply it.

The same check also refused to restore a backup unless the appliance had a working internet
connection, even though everything needed for the restore was already on the device.

The appliance now tells Home Assistant that these are deliberate, every time it checks, so a
restore or a repair cannot silently switch it back on.

Nothing about how your home behaves changes.
